findings.title: Inefficient size allocation pattern
findings.description: The BondingCurve account structure in the smart contract allocates an excessive amount of space (SIZE+175 bytes) per account, which exceeds actual storage requirements even after accounting for future upgrades involving creator fees. This inefficient allocation is caused by hardcoding an unnecessarily large buffer in the account size definition, leading to suboptimal use of on-chain resources. An attacker cannot directly exploit this issue, but malicious actors could potentially amplify the economic burden by creating a large number of accounts, increasing overall network costs. The impact includes higher rent fees for users and increased storage load on validators, resulting in reduced cost-efficiency and scalability for the protocol.

findings.title: Fee vault is made rent-exempt even if no fee shall be collected
findings.description: The program makes the creator fee vault rent-exempt during buy and sell transactions whenever a creator is present, regardless of whether the actual fee amount is zero. This is caused by the lack of a conditional check for a non-zero fee before executing the rent exemption logic. As a result, unnecessary rent-exemption operations are performed even when no fee is collected, leading to avoidable transaction costs. An attacker could exploit this by repeatedly conducting zero-fee transactions to increase cost overhead for users or to bloat transaction fees. The impact is limited to increased transaction costs (approximately 0.00089088 SOL per transaction), which, while small per instance, can accumulate and degrade user experience over time.
